q-43908.name: Question 1
q-43908.problem:
An inner product on $V={R}^{3}$ is defined as $⟨x,y⟩={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+4{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+7{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.$ 
Calculate the norm of the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ under this inner product.
q-43908.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $v$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖=\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $‖v‖$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{3\cdot 3+4\cdot ((-2)\cdot (-2))+7\cdot (0\cdot 0)} \\  & =\sqrt{9+16} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

q-97423.name: Question 6
q-97423.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(0)y(0)+x(1)y(1)+x(2)y(2).
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $p(t)=3t-2{t}^{2}.$
q-97423.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $p(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $p(t)=3t-2{t}^{2},$ we obtain

$$
p(0)=0,\,p(1)=1,\,p(2)=-2.
$$

Computing $‖p(t)‖$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖ & =\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{p(0)p(0)+p(1)p(1)+p(2)p(2)} \\  & =\sqrt{[p(0)]^{2}+[p(1)]^{2}+[p(2)]^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+1+4} \\  & =\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-141170.problem:
Let $V=C[-1,1]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[-1,1],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{-1}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)=1-t.$
q-141170.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(1-t)^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}({t}^{2}-2t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={(\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}-{t}^{2}+t)|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{3}-1+1)-(\frac{(-1)^{3}}{3}-(-1)^{2}+(-1)) \\  & =\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{\frac{8}{3}}=2\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}.
$$

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1.$
q-97712.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }\,(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1)^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }\,(4{cos}^{2}⁡t+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }((2+2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }(3+2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(3t+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t){|}_{\pi }^{2\pi } \\  & =(6\pi +0+0)-(3\pi +0+0) \\  & =3\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we made use of the trigonometric identity 

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡t=\frac{1+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖f(t)‖ & =\sqrt{3\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Let V=C[π,2π] be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on [π,2π], equipped with the inner product

⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=∫π2πx(t)y(t)dt.

Calculate the norm of the vector f(t)=2cos⁡t+1.

a
3π
b
9π+5
c
3π
d
3π+5
e
π
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The norm of a vector f(t) with respect to an inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ is defined as

‖f(t)‖=⟨f(t),f(t)⟩.

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

⟨f(t),f(t)⟩=∫π2π(f(t))2dt=∫π2π(2cos⁡t+1)2dt=∫π2π(4cos2⁡t+4cos⁡t+1)dt=∫π2π((2+2cos⁡2t)+4cos⁡t+1)dt=∫π2π(3+2cos⁡2t+4cos⁡t)dt=(3t+sin⁡2t+4sin⁡t)|π2π=(6π+0+0)−(3π+0+0)=3π.

Note that we made use of the trigonometric identity

cos2⁡t=1+cos⁡2t2.

Finally then,

‖f(t)‖=3π.

q-42727.name: Question 13
q-42727.problem:
Let $V=C[0,1]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,1],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)=t+2.$
q-42727.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(t+2)^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({t}^{2}+4t+4)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={(\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}+2{t}^{2}+4t)|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}+2+4 \\  & =\frac{19}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{\frac{19}{3}}.
$$

q-97713.name: Question 14
q-97713.problem:
Let $V=C[-1,1]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[-1,1],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{-1}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)={t}^{2}+1.$
q-97713.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}({t}^{2}+1)^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}({t}^{4}+2{t}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={(\frac{{t}^{5}}{5}+\frac{2{t}^{3}}{3}+t)|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{5}+\frac{2}{3}+1)-(-\frac{1}{5}-\frac{2}{3}-1) \\  & =\frac{2}{5}+\frac{4}{3}+2 \\  & =\frac{56}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{\frac{56}{15}}=2\sqrt{\frac{14}{15}}.
$$

q-42763.name: Question 15
q-42763.problem:
Let $V=C[0,2]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,2],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{2}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)=t+{t}^{2}.$
q-42763.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(t+{t}^{2})^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({t}^{2}+2{t}^{3}+{t}^{4})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={(\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}+\frac{{t}^{4}}{2}+\frac{{t}^{5}}{5})|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}+8+\frac{32}{5} \\  & =\frac{256}{15}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$

Question 17
?

Let V=C[0,1] be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on [0,1], equipped with the inner product

⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=∫01x(t)y(t)dt.

Normalize the vector f(t)=t−1.

a
t−1
b
32(t−1)
c
2(t−1)
d
4(t−1)
e
3(t−1)

EXPLANATION

The norm of a vector f(t) with respect to an inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ is defined as

‖f(t)‖=⟨f(t),f(t)⟩.

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

⟨f(t),f(t)⟩=∫01(t−1)2dt=∫01(t2−2t+1)dt=(t33−t2+t)|01=13−1+1=13

Therefore,

‖f(t)‖=13.

To normalize the vector f(t), we divide f(t) by its norm ‖f(t)‖:

u(t)=f(t)‖f(t)‖=t−1(13)=3(t−1)

q-43926.name: Question 18
q-43926.problem:
Let $V=C[0,1]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,1],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Normalize the vector $f(t)=1-\sqrt{t}.$
q-43926.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{(1-\sqrt{t})}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\,(1-2\sqrt{t}+t),\text{d}t \\  & ={(t-\frac{4{t}^{3/2}}{3}+\frac{{t}^{2}}{2})|}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =1-\frac{4}{3}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
‖f(t)‖=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}.
$$

To normalize the vector $f(t),$ we divide $f(t)$ by its norm $‖f(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\frac{f(t)}{‖f(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{(1-\sqrt{t})}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}} \\  & =\sqrt{6}(1-\sqrt{t})\end{aligned}
$$

q-141174.name: Question 19
q-141174.problem:
An inner product on $V={R}^{3}$ is defined as $⟨x,y⟩={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.$ 

Normalize the  vector  $v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ under this inner product.
q-141174.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $v$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖=\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨v,v⟩ & =2\cdot 2+3\cdot 1\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot (-1) \\  & =4+3+1 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{8}=2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

To normalize the vector $v$, we divide $v$ by its norm $‖v‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{v}{‖v‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

An inner product on V=R3 is defined as ⟨x,y⟩=x1y1+3x2y2+x3y3.

Normalize the vector v=[21−1] under this inner product.

a
12[21−1]
b
24[21−1]
c
36[21−1]
d
33[21−1]
e
22[21−1]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The norm of a vector v with respect to an inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ is defined as

‖v‖=⟨v,v⟩.

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

⟨v,v⟩=2⋅2+3⋅1⋅1+(−1)⋅(−1)=4+3+1=8.

Therefore,

‖v‖=8=22.

To normalize the vector v, we divide v by its norm ‖v‖:

u=v‖v‖=122[21−1]=24[21−1]

q-97726.problem:
An inner product on $V={R}^{3}$ is defined as $⟨x,y⟩=2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.$ 

Normalize the  vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ under this inner product.
q-97726.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $v$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖=\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨v,v⟩ & =2\cdot (3\cdot 3)+2\cdot (2\cdot 2)+(-3)\cdot (-3) \\  & =18+8+9 \\  & =35.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{35}.\end{aligned}
$$

To normalize the vector $v$, we divide $v$ by its norm $‖v‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{v}{‖v‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{35}}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{35}}{35}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

An inner product on V=R3 is defined as ⟨x,y⟩=2x1y1+2x2y2+x3y3.

Normalize the vector v=[32−3] under this inner product.

a
2222[32−3]
b
3535[32−3]
c
77[32−3]
d
22[32−3]
e
122[32−3]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The norm of a vector v with respect to an inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ is defined as

‖v‖=⟨v,v⟩.

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

⟨v,v⟩=2⋅(3⋅3)+2⋅(2⋅2)+(−3)⋅(−3)=18+8+9=35.

Therefore,

‖v‖=35.

To normalize the vector v, we divide v by its norm ‖v‖:

u=v‖v‖=135[32−3]=3535[32−3]
